deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page sets up linear isotropic elasticity for a cylindrical rod whose axis is x and whose cross-section lies in the (y,z)-plane. The next page treats extension and torsion of a cylinder of radius R and length l (pi*Delta*R^2*l, 'Torsion', torsion parameter m). That page also has upside-down calculations with logarithms and integrals such as int_0^oo (1-e^{-x})/x dx. This makes it likely, though not certain, that the setting is wire experiments of the Weber/Kohlrausch type.

(1) Strain energy in principal dilatations.
- lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3 are the principal dilatations (principal strains).
- delta P is the virtual work ('Gesammtmoment') of the internal forces of the body:
  delta P = -∫ rho dV [ (a l1 + b l2 + b l3) δl1 + (b l1 + a l2 + b l3) δl2 + (b l1 + b l2 + a l3) δl3 ], with a > b > 0.
- This is an exact variation. Setting e1 = l1+l2+l3 and e2 = l2 l3 + l3 l1 + l1 l2 (my notation):
  -P = ∫ rho dV [ (a/2)(l1^2+l2^2+l3^2) + b e2 ] = ∫ rho dV [ (a/2) e1^2 - (a-b) e2 ].
- Riemann writes 4P = ∫ rho dV [ 2a e1^2 - 4(a-b) e2 ]. Up to the overall sign (energy versus work of the internal forces), this is exactly 4 times the above.

(2) Displacements.
- x, y, z are the rectangular coordinates of an arbitrary material point before the deformation; x+u, y+v, z+w are its coordinates after.
- To first order, e1 and e2 are the first and second invariants of the symmetric strain tensor:
  e1 = u_x + v_y + w_z;
  e2 = (u_x v_y + v_y w_z + w_z u_x) - (1/4)[ (v_z+w_y)^2 + (w_x+u_z)^2 + (u_y+v_x)^2 ].
- Implicit step (mine): u_x v_y + v_y w_z + w_z u_x = (e1^2 - u_x^2 - v_y^2 - w_z^2)/2.
- Substituting:
  4·(energy) = ∫ rho dV { (a-b)[ (v_z+w_y)^2 + (w_x+u_z)^2 + (u_y+v_x)^2 + 2(u_x^2 + v_y^2 + w_z^2) ] + 2b e1^2 },
  which is the line on the page.
- Modern reading: energy density = (b/2) e1^2 + ((a-b)/2) eps:eps. Hence the Lamé constants are lambda = b and mu = (a-b)/2, so a = lambda + 2mu.
- The condition a > b > 0 means mu > 0 and lambda > 0.
- Next-page consistency: the coefficient (a-b)(a+2b)/(a+b) there is exactly Young's modulus mu(3lambda+2mu)/(lambda+mu). The torsion term (1/2)R^2(a-b) m δm is mu R^2 m δm.

(3) Complex coordinates in the cross-section.
- Set p = y+iz, q = y-iz, pi = v+iw, chi = v-iw, with ∂_p = (∂_y - i∂_z)/2 and ∂_q = (∂_y + i∂_z)/2.
- Then pi_p + chi_q = v_y + w_z.
- Also 4 pi_q chi_p = (v_y - w_z)^2 + (v_z + w_y)^2. Hence 2v_y^2 + 2w_z^2 + (v_z+w_y)^2 = 4 pi_q chi_p + (pi_p + chi_q)^2.
- Since 2u_q + pi_x = (u_y+v_x) + i(u_z+w_x) and 2u_p + chi_x is its conjugate:
  (u_y+v_x)^2 + (u_z+w_x)^2 = (2u_q + pi_x)(2u_p + chi_x).
- So the transverse part of the energy density is written through the modulus of complex (Wirtinger-type) derivatives.

(4) Polar form.
- Set p = r e^{i phi} and pi = rho e^{i psi} - p. Thus rho e^{i psi} = (y+v) + i(z+w): (rho, psi) are the polar coordinates of the displaced point. A marginal note seems to introduce psi = phi + (angle).
- With f = p + pi = rho e^{i psi}: pi_q = f_q and chi_p = conj(f_q).
- In polar coordinates ∂_q = (1/2) e^{i phi}(∂_r + (i/r)∂_phi), giving
  4 pi_q chi_p = (rho_r - (rho/r) psi_phi)^2 + (rho psi_r + rho_phi/r)^2.
- Likewise pi_p + chi_q = 2 Re f_p - 2 = cos(phi-psi)(rho_r + rho psi_phi/r) + sin(phi-psi)(rho psi_r - rho_phi/r) - 2.
- Riemann rewrites this as
  ∂_r(rho cos(phi-psi)) + (1/r)∂_phi(rho sin(psi-phi)) + (rho/r)cos(phi-psi) - 2 = (1/r)∂_r(r rho cos(phi-psi)) + (1/r)∂_phi(rho sin(psi-phi)) - 2.
- This is the polar-coordinate divergence of the in-plane deformed position field (radial component rho cos(psi-phi), angular component rho sin(psi-phi)), minus 2 = div of the identity map in 2D.
- The shear factor is (2u_q + pi_x)·e^{∓i phi} = u_r + i u_phi/r + (rho_x + i rho psi_x) e^{i(psi-phi)}.

The purpose is to express the elastic energy of a circular cylinder in cylindrical coordinates, ready for the torsion and extension computations on the next page.
errors: Sign convention: delta P as defined is the work of the internal forces, so P = -(energy). The line written as 4P = ∫[2a e1^2 - 4(a-b)e2] is really -4P (that is, 4 x strain energy). This is harmless, since only the quadratic form matters.

The factor multiplying (2 ∂u/∂q + ∂pi/∂x) should be e^{-phi i}, not e^{+phi i}. With p = y+zi, 2u_q = u_y + i u_z = e^{i phi}(u_r + i u_phi/r) and pi_x = (rho_x + i rho psi_x) e^{i psi}. Only the modulus enters the energy, so this possible slip (or an unseen minus sign in the exponent) does not affect anything.

The quadratic invariant line should contain (∂u/∂x ∂v/∂y + ∂v/∂y ∂w/∂z + ∂w/∂z ∂u/∂x). If the manuscript really reads ∂u/∂y ∂v/∂z, that is a slip, but the following line is computed correctly with the right invariant.

Mixed exact/linear treatment: rho, psi are exact polar coordinates of the deformed point, while u, v, w enter a linearized (small-strain) energy. The identities on the page are exact algebraic identities, so there is no error, but the energy itself is only valid for small displacements.

results.what: Isotropic strain energy as a quadratic form in principal dilatations with two constants a > b > 0, rewritten as (b/2)(div u)^2 + ((a-b)/2) eps:eps
results.modern_name: Two-constant (Lamé) isotropic linear elasticity; lambda = b, mu = (a-b)/2
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy (1828), Lamé & Clapeyron (1833), Green (1839, energy formulation)

results.what: Expression of the second strain invariant and of the energy in displacement derivatives
Use of complex conjugate coordinates p = y+iz, q = y-iz and pi = v+iw, chi = v-iw to write the transverse strain energy as |∂pi/∂q|^2 plus (Re ∂pi/∂p)^2 terms
results.modern_name: Wirtinger derivatives in plane elasticity (complex-variable form of the strain energy)
results.usually_credited_to: Complex methods in elasticity: Kolosov (1909), Muskhelishvili (1930s). Wirtinger calculus: Riemann's 1851 dissertation, Poincaré, Wirtinger (1927)

results.what: Polar-coordinate expression of the in-plane dilatation as a divergence of the deformed position field: (1/r)∂_r(r rho cos(phi-psi)) + (1/r)∂_phi(rho sin(psi-phi)) - 2
Implied (via next page) effective modulus (a-b)(a+2b)/(a+b) for simple extension

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard 1830s-1850s isotropic elasticity with two constants, set up for torsion/extension of a cylinder. The only mildly distinctive feature is the systematic use of conjugate complex coordinates (∂/∂p, ∂/∂q) to organize the transverse strain energy. This prefigures later complex-variable methods in elasticity, but here it is only an algebraic bookkeeping device, entirely in Riemann's known style from his 1851 dissertation; no complex potentials or new elastic results appear. Riemann's unpublished interest in elasticity (probably linked to Weber/Kohlrausch wire experiments) is a minor biographical detail.

Second invariant line: the bilinear terms should be (∂u/∂x ∂v/∂y + ∂v/∂y ∂w/∂z + ...), not ∂u/∂y ∂v/∂z; check the manuscript.
4P line: the manuscript has a struck leading symbol and possibly a sign. Mathematically the bracket is 2a(λ1+λ2+λ3)^2 - 4(a-b)(λ2λ3+λ3λ1+λ1λ2), consistent with the transcription.
Margin 'ψ = φ+ϑ' is very uncertain; the image shows something like 'ψ = φ+ψ' or '4 = φ4' struck/overwritten.
